short: The first self-propelled gun: a tracked mount that could fire the howitzer it carried.
full:
The problem the Gun Carrier answered was that artillery could not follow an advance across its own barrage's craters. Designed by Major Walter Gordon Wilson and Major Gregg and approved in July 1916, it was a tracked chassis with the engine amidships and an open cradle at the front onto which a 60-pounder gun or a 6-inch howitzer was winched, wheels and all. The howitzer could be fired from the vehicle without unloading it, which makes the Gun Carrier the first modern self-propelled gun. Forty-eight were built.

They reached France in July 1917 and were used at Pilckem Ridge at the opening of Third Ypres, but the tactical case was never made and the guns were mostly dismounted for conventional use. What the vehicles proved good at was load carrying: one could move seven tons of ammunition to a forward dump through shellfire, work that would otherwise take some 290 men. The two gun carrier companies were formally converted to supply companies in June 1918 and served in that role to the armistice.
